What Is Māyā?

Satyanārāyaṇa Dāsa Bābājī speaks with Rajiv Malhotra about the correct understanding of māyā.

The word māyā is commonly translated as "illusion," but this is only a partial understanding of what māyā is. First of all, māyā is not merely an impersonal force; it is personified as Māyādevi, who plays a significant role in spiritual cosmology.

Māyā also possesses two primary potencies that serve different functions: the āvaraṇa śakti (the covering or veiling potency) and the vikṣepa śakti (the bewildering potency). These potencies influence us in distinct ways. The āvaraṇa śakti causes us to forget our true spiritual identity, which is the conscious ātmā, while the vikṣepa śakti deludes us into thinking the body and mind are who we are. Māyā also manifests an external world of objects that further deludes and distracts us.

However, māyā cannot perform these two functions without the support of Bhagavān (Kṛṣṇa), as illusion must always be rooted in reality. So māyā ultimately has its support in Bhagavān, and therefore, if you want to overcome the delusion caused by Māyā, you have to take shelter of Bhagavān. Hence, Kṛṣṇa saying in the Bhagavad-gītā:

daivī hy eṣā guṇa-mayī
mama māyā duratyayā
mām eva ye prapadyante
māyām etāṁ taranti te

Translation:
This divine external potency of Mine (māyā), constituted of the three guṇas (sattva, rajas and tamas), is indeed very difficult to surmount. Yet those who take shelter in me alone, can cross over this māyā.

सत्यं सत्यं पुनः सत्यं सत्यमेव पुनः पुनः । 
विना राधिको प्रसादे मत्प्रसादो न विद्यते  ।।
